proposition: Niʿmatullahi hagiography claims Ibn Turka and Yazdī sought out Niʿmat Allāh Valī at Kūhbanān and, at his direction, became disciples of Akhlāṭī and learned jafr; the Savāniḥ version adds Qāsim-i Anvār, Pīr Tāj Gīl and a roof collapsing, and makes Niʿmat Allāh's master a disciple of Akhlāṭī. MK reads both as hagiographic strategy to establish Akhlāṭī's mastery and then Niʿmat Allāh's greater one.

mediation.note: written at the request of Niʿmat Allāh II to honour Niʿmat Allāh; wants credit for initiating the Akhlāṭī discipleship

mediation.who: Ṣunʿ Allāh Niʿmatullāhī, Savāniḥ al-Ayyām, via Mufīd Mustawfī (fl. 1091/1680)
mediation.note: known only through a Safavid compiler who also mixed in Shūshtarī; more fabulous, wants Niʿmat Allāh's Shiʿism
